messages:
Anna M: quick sync — need final messaging for next week's webinar plus the 1-pager for field. goal: 3 clear knockouts vs cloud AI platforms, generic LLM APIs, and infra vendors. can we ship a rebut matrix by EOD?
Mike G: sales asks for short, deployable lines they can paste into emails/notes. priority: latency story, predictable unit economics, and rollout/ops differences.
Jess L: agreed. proposing 3 condensed hooks (one per competitor class) then 2 supporting facts each. quick draft below — open to edits.
Jess L: 
```
Hook A (cloud AI platforms): "Predictable latency at scale — not bursty behind shared control planes."
  - Supporting: tail-latency SLOs + automatic fallback to reserved capacity.
Hook B (LLM APIs): "Same API, better economics — optimize batching & cache automatically."
  - Supporting: token/unit cost delta vs typical API routing.
Hook C (infrastructure vendors): "Ship inference, not ops — unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private."
  - Supporting: rollout primitives, per-route tracing, and out-of-the-box KV caching.
```
Raj P: those are good. please avoid absolute numeric claims without context. for bench claims we should say "up to" and link to the appendix. ops needs the exact test harness for any numbers.
Taylor K: marketing note — field wants 1-liner rebut lines for SDRs and a slightly longer paragraph for AE playbooks. also a short FAQ: procurement asks about SLAs and private deployment security.
Jen S: i can draft the SDR snippets. quick templates: 
- "If latency spikes under load, we route to dedicated pools — customers see stable P95s."
- "We reduce per-token costs with prefix caching and batching; you keep the API contract."
Anna M: @Jen S perfect. can you make 3 versions: short (1 line), email (2-3 lines), and slide-friendly (bullet)?
Jen S: on it. ETA 3pm PT. :thumbsup:
Mike G: small ask for the webinar narrative: open with a customer problem (bursting costs / unpredictable latency), then demo routing/fallback + cost panel, end with rollout story (how to pin versions and A/B).
Raj P: for the demo we'll show a live failover to dedicated for a spike and the rollback/rollout in console. product will provide a trimmed recording if live is risky.
Jess L: copy edits to avoid jargon: swap "KV cache" for "response prefix caching" in public-facing lines. keep technical terms in the appendix.
Anna M: noted. can we agree on 4 rebut one-liners now so we can populate the battle sheet?
Mike G: here are 4 candidates: 
1) "Consistent tail latency — engineered routing, not best-effort sharing."
2) "Lower predictable unit cost through workload-aware batching & caching."
3) "Same API surface; flexible deployments (hosted, dedicated, private)."
4) "Rollouts & tracing built for production — canary/A-B with automatic fallback."
Taylor K: reorder for SDR use: 2,1,4,3. start with econ hook in cold outreach.
Jess L: tweak 3 to "Same API; deploy where you need it (hosted, reserved, VPC)."
Anna M: ok final checklist: 
- Jen to produce 3 snippet lengths (due 3pm PT)
- Raj to sign off on any numeric language and provide bench appendix link
- Jess to run one-pager copy review by design
- Mike/Taylor to run quick field test with 3 SDRs tomorrow AM
ops-bot: Reminder: shared doc created at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xEXAMPLE (marketing/webinar/battle-sheet)
Jen S: putting drafts into that doc now.
Raj P: i'll add bench notes and lab harness in the appendix by 5pm.
Anna M: perfect — i'll stitch and publish the battle sheet to the sales drive once Raj and Jess sign off. thanks team! :rocket:
